reviews.text:
Great for snow birds/families. We thoroughly enjoyed our time in Fort Lauderdale at the W Residences. Overall great but a few things to know to make it better. It took a few days to get settled as we were initially stuck dealing with Vacasa call center which went round and round. Once we made contact with Rozanna (local Vacasa rep) she took action and worked hard to fix issues on our behalf. This place is better for longer term rentals. It has a full kitchen and was comfortable. Exactly what you would expect from a W.

Caveat: it’s best suited for 4 adults in two king beds. The pull out sofas are not for sleeping. Rozanna was able to get us a xl twin roll away about a week into pur stay. Hopefully this makes it much easier for next guest.

Caveat 2- We thought when we initially rented parking was included but later found out, closer to arrival, it wasn’t. So we used Uber and we rented from Avis downstairs as needed and would return car at end of day to avoid paying for parking which worked well for our needs. Not a big deal but wish I would have been prepared. 

Caveat 3
For longer term rentals it would be helpful if they included mid or weekly cleaning. It’s impossible to wash towels and sheets in the small washing machine and dryer. I had to dry one towel per hour. The owner of the place can authorize a cleaning for about half of what we paid Vacasa for mid stay cleaning. I know other air b&b’s provide mid stay cleaning.

Again- I Rozanna and her team were responsive and easy to deal with once we were able to connect with her.

We have been booked in this cabin for a year. It was my dads 70th birthday. Our check in time was 4pm. At 12 pm we get an email from Vacasa stating our check in time was moved to 6pm. No biggie, we were tired and ready to check in but we could stop and get groceries first. We got stuck in Atlanta traffic and actually didn’t get to blue ridge closer to 7:30 and had gotten another message from vacasa stating that our check in was now moved to 8pm. We stopped by the grocery store and got groceries and then went to the cabin. It was filthy. Clearly it had not been cleaned yet. We sent a message to Vacasa and they said the cleaning company was delayed and they would be there in 20 minutes. We had been traveling all day and were exhausted but we understood that this town had a lot of evacuees from the hurricane in Florida and NC recently so we were trying to be patient. The cleaning crew was a couple with their child and this was their 13th clean of the day. The occupants before us had left the cabin pretty dirty unfortunately. Unbeknownst to us, the dishwasher had been broken. The cleaners were unaware, so we throught the previous occupants had left us a sinkful of dirty dishes. We helped (we thought) the cleaners by loading the dishwasher and starting it, but it ended up being broken and that didn’t get communicated to the cleaners so inevitably we eneded up having to wash that whole load of dishes (yay for vacation!) The maintenance man said it was irreparable and they couldn’t replace it while we stayed. And I’m sure it won’t
Be replaced by the next guests stay either. 
The Linen company needs to be replaced. The towels are terrible. Water repellent. They leave white lint balls all over you and your clothes. The sheets were fine. 
We had ants in the downstairs bathroom and the very bottom bunk room. I’m guessing that’s what the bottles of raid were left on the game table for. 
The kids really really enjoyed the game room and the downstairs bunk area. They’re teens and that gave them their own space. 
We enjoyed the decks and porch areas. There were a lot of posts outside that need repairs and the cabin could use a deep cleaning inside and out. The cabinets are dirty and you can tell
The cleanings are done very quickly to get the cabin turned over between guests. I know our cleaners were rushed because we were inside the cabin while they were cleaning. But it definitely needs a good deep clean. 
The vents need to be changed. We traveled with 2 two year olds and had to put a chair over at least 2 of the floor vents. They could have fallen in them very easily because they’re broken. 
Honestly, if I owned this cabin, I would choose a different management company because I like Vacasa is doing them a disservice. This is my 3rd and last time renting with Vacasa.

reviews.text:
Absolute Worst Management Company Ever. I recently had the misfortune of dealing with Vacasa Vacation Rental Management, and I cannot stress enough how poorly run this company is. It is abundantly clear that they are unprofitable and on a fast track towards bankruptcy. This pervasive attitude of failure and despair permeates every aspect of their business.

Their customer service is nothing short of a joke. Whether you’re dealing with their poorly scripted AI bots or their human representatives (who might as well be robots), the experience is equally frustrating and unhelpful. Vacasa has effectively removed hospitality from the hospitality business, leaving customers feeling neglected and disrespected.

For any self-respecting homeowner considering contracting with Vacasa, I strongly advise against it. Their incompetence and disregard for customer satisfaction are unmatched. They are so abysmal in their operations that I am certain many people end up trashing the properties in revenge for the appalling way they have been treated.

To make matters worse, Vacasa CEO Rob Greyber received a $2 million bonus for overseeing this train wreck and a staggering 90% drop in stock value. Vacasa chases failure like it’s their destiny … and it is.

Save yourself the headache and steer clear of Vacasa. They are a disaster waiting to happen, and no one should have to endure the level of incompetence and disrespect that they dish out on a daily basis.
